title: Device control-plane structured error
description: Structured error envelope for device control-plane HTTP routes. Workspace maps code device_busy to a UserError (never a silent queue or Ninja fallback). Shape is frozen for epic #818 / M0.2 #828. additionalProperties:false is intentional: new codes and new optional fields are additive, but they must be declared in this file when introduced (validators reject undeclared fields); existing fields may not change meaning.

code.description: Stable machine-readable code. Frozen registry: device_busy (409, active job holds the device), fence_violation (409, wrong/expired claim_token), job_terminal (409, job already terminal including lost), log_seq_conflict (409, seq reused with different content), invalid_key (401, missing/unknown/disabled device or control key), enrollment_token_invalid (401), enrollment_token_expired (401), enrollment_token_consumed (401), device_disabled (403, device exists but not active), out_of_scope (403, control key does not target this device), unknown_job (404), unknown_device (404, no device for id in caller scope), unknown_control_key (404, no control key for id in caller scope), device_not_active (409, lifecycle precondition not met, e.g. rotate before enroll), control_key_inactive (409, rotation requested for a revoked or expired control key — replace instead), permission_denied (403, user lacks can_execute_devices/can_manage_config), unauthenticated (401, no user credential or control key presented where either is required), script_too_large (413), payload_too_large (413), invalid_parameter (422). Additive codes are recorded here when introduced.

message.description: Operator-readable explanation. Must never embed raw key material or full script bodies.

retryable.description: True only when an identical retry may succeed without a new logical request decision (for example a transient blip). device_busy, fence_violation, and job_terminal are never retryable in place; busy requires a new job create after the device frees up, and fence/terminal outcomes require an explicit new job id when retry is intended.

job_id.description: Required when code is device_busy: the id of the active job holding the device. Optional elsewhere.

allOf.$comment: device_busy must carry job_id and is never retryable in place.
Fence/terminal rejections are never retryable in place; retry means a new job id.
